news.summary_en: Suzhou-based MegaRobo Technologies has raised nearly $200 million in a new financing round led by the Oman Investment Authority (OIA), with participation from Asia Investment Capital, Granite Asia, Sinovation Ventures, and CMB International. The capital will support the R&D of its proprietary 'One Intelligence Stack' and the global expansion of its AI-for-Science infrastructure, enabling autonomous execution and learning in complex physical scientific environments.
paragraphs: AI's Next Frontier Is the Physical World. Science Is Where It Begins.

SUZHOU, China, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MegaRobo Technologies (MegaRobo), a technology company building Intelligence Infrastructure for the Physical World, today announced that it has raised nearly US$200 million in a new financing round joined by Oman Investment Authority (OIA), the sovereign wealth fund of the Sultanate of Oman. And existing investors Asia Investment Capital, Granite Asia and Sinovation Ventures continued to back the company, with new participation from CMB International.

The new financing will support MegaRobo's continued investment in core technology, the global expansion of its AI for Science business, and the development of infrastructure that enables AI to operate in increasingly complex physical environments.

The first generation of AI learned primarily from digital information - text, images, video and code. The next generation will increasingly learn by interacting with the physical world: acting on real systems, observing outcomes, and using those outcomes to decide what to do next.

In science, that means moving beyond reading papers, predicting structures or generating molecules. AI must also be able to design experiments, execute them in real laboratories, observe the results and learn from what happens.

MegaRobo is building the infrastructure for that transition. Its proprietary One Intelligence Stack connects intelligence with execution - bringing together models and agents, data, workflows, software, scientific instruments, robotics, automation and real-world feedback in a single reusable technology foundation.
One Intelligence Stack. Across Complex Physical Systems.THINK -DESIGN -EXECUTE -OBSERVE -LEARN

Science is the first proving ground for this architecture because it requires AI to do more than analyze information. Scientific discovery depends on an ongoing loop between reasoning, design, physical experimentation, observation and learning - often under conditions where the answer is not known in advance.

MegaRobo is applying this architecture to scientific discovery and pharmaceutical R&D through an integrated AI for Science infrastructure that combines AI, scientific computing, experimental execution, data and R&D decision-making.

The company has delivered products and technologies to more than 500 customers, including leading global pharmaceutical companies, drug discovery organizations, biotechnology companies and research institutions. Its systems support key stages of discovery and development, including early research, target and mechanism discovery, drug screening and candidate optimization.

Through Megalaxy Lab, MegaRobo is also making real-world experimentation increasingly programmable. Researchers and AI agents can configure experiments, route them to automated laboratory systems, track execution, and receive structured, machine-readable results that can feed directly into the next cycle of scientific reasoning. Megalaxy Lab has served more than 200 customers.

MegaRobo is now extending this capability to the global AI for Science community. Together with industry partners including Tencent Cloud and Twist Bioscience, the company has launched Poreva Open, a global AI protein design challenge open to all models and technical approaches. Megalaxy Lab will provide wet-lab validation for more than 10,000 protein design sequences, creating an opportunity for innovators worldwide to test their models against real experimental results. By opening up large-scale experimental validation to the global research community, Poreva Open aims to help establish a common benchmark for AI-driven protein design.

This marks a shift in how scientific infrastructure is accessed: from laboratory work organized mainly as individual projects toward experimental capacity that can increasingly be standardized, automated and called on demand by scientists, software and AI agents.

Science is where MegaRobo is starting, but the underlying architecture is designed for other complex physical systems as well. Wherever AI must interact with instruments, machines, materials, processes and real-world feedback, the same core challenge appears: intelligence must connect to execution, and execution must generate observations that intelligence can learn from.

MegaRobo is developing One Intelligence Stack as a common technology foundation for this interaction - not as a collection of isolated AI applications or automation products, but as infrastructure that enables AI to act, observe and learn across complex physical environments.

Daniel Huang, Founder and CEO of MegaRobo, said: "The first generation of AI learned from humanity's accumulated knowledge. The next generation will increasingly learn by acting in the physical world - through experiments, production and continuous feedback. That shift changes AI from a system that interprets the world into one that can help create new knowledge, materials, processes and products. MegaRobo is building the infrastructure for that transition."

Liu Erh Fei, Founding Partner and CEO of Asia Investment Capital, said:"As a long-term shareholder, we have seen MegaRobo continuously drive innovation, earn the trust of its customers and translate its technological capabilities into commercial applications. Its ability to integrate AI, software and hardware, together with its experience in scientific research and advanced manufacturing, underpins our continued investment. We look forward to continuing to support MegaRobo as it further strengthens its product and technology platforms and serves more customers worldwide."

The new round builds on MegaRobo's long-standing backing from leading global investors and strategic partners. To date, the company has raised approximately US$600 million across multiple financing rounds. This includes a nearly US$300 million Series C round co-led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Asia Investment Capital and Granite Asia, with participation from Pavilion Capital, a part of Temasek's Seviora Group. Long-term investors such as Sinovation Ventures, Joy Capital and MPCi have continued to support MegaRobo through multiple stages of its growth. Earlier industry investors also include WuXi AppTec and Bosch Ventures.

Together, this diverse group of technology, financial and industrial partners reflect MegaRobo's evolution into a global technology company with deep capabilities spanning scientific discovery and complex physical systems. Its continued expansion across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia will accelerate the global scale-up of intelligence infrastructure for the physical world.

paragraphs: CHICAGO, Nov 18 (Reuters) - The state of Arizona has opened a criminal investigation into OpenAI and other AI companies relating to the "apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents," Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes said Wednesday.
A criminal investigation does not necessarily mean charges will be brought. Mayes said her office was investigating whether Arizona state law was being violated on an ongoing basis.
"The state of Arizona is very worried about this, and we are looking at it from multiple angles," Mayes told a press conference in Chicago.
Mayes declined to identify the other companies her office was investigating. She said her office had been in contact with Arizona banks, but declined to name them or give their responses.
A spokesperson for OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The banking industry has become increasingly concerned that sophisticated AI agents could harm the banking system and the institutions trusted to hold people's wealth. Reuters reported last month that major US banks have been blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside customer accounts and making transactions.

Mayes' comments come two days after California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI for allegedly developing a dangerous product without adequate safety procedures or oversight after reports that its AI models had carried out cyberattacks independently.

OpenAI did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on that lawsuit, but the company has acknowledged a general need for more transparency around rogue AI behavior and said it was reinforcing its safeguards. On September 16, the company published a new framework for disclosing such incidents, saying it would err on the side of transparency "even when significance is uncertain."
This story was originally published November 18, 2026 at 8:36 PM.

news.title: Intel signs first external customer for advanced 18A chips
news.title_en: Intel signs first external customer for advanced 18A chips
news.author: Katie Tarasov
news.content_snippet:
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Wednesday that the company has signed the first outside customer for its 18A chips.

"Resilient supply on the foundry is very important,"Tan said at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas. "And then 18A, I'm involved in production and we just signed the first customer,"Tan added, without naming the debut client.

It's a milestone moment for Intel in its five-year effort to take on chip manufacturing leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. After years of missteps
news.summary_en: Intel's CEO announced at the TomorrowX Summit that the company has signed its first external customer for the 18A process node, which entered risk production in June. This milestone aims to validate Intel's foundry turnaround strategy and alleviate capacity constraints for hyperscalers currently over-reliant on TSMC.
paragraphs: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Wednesday that the company has signed the first outside customer for its 18A chips.

"Resilient supply on the foundry is very important,"Tan said at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas. "And then 18A, I'm involved in production and we just signed the first customer,"Tan added, without naming the debut client.

It's a milestone moment for Intel in its five-year effort to take on chip manufacturing leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. After years of missteps and low yields, Intel touted 18A as key to a turnaround that would finally convert the company into a competitive chip manufacturer for non-Intel products.
"It's a huge win for foundry,"Creative Strategies analyst Ben Bajarin told CNBC in an interview.

Pushkar Ranade, Intel's technology chief, clarified on X that the external customer had signed up for Intel's 18A-P manufacturing process node, which went into risk production in June. In May, reports indicated that Apple and Intel were closing in on a deal to use Intel's foundry to make some of the chips for Apple devices.

Intel's stock has lost more than half its value since the end of September, with most of that plunge coming late last month after the company said revenue this quarter will be at least $1 billion shy of analysts' estimates due to a PC sales slump and supply chain challenges.
In considering who the customer may be, Bajarin pointed to Nvidia, Apple or the major hyperscalers that make their own custom processors.
"Amazon, Microsoft and Google are struggling to get capacity for their CPU ambitions at TSMC,"he said. "So it makes sense that you go somewhere for at least some capacity."

Tan said in late October that he sees the global market for server processors increasing as much as five times over the next five years to about $200 billion, but that Intel can't currently meet customer demand.

Wall Street has turned on Intel of late after the chipmaker had become a top trade starting in the middle of last year. The U.S. government took a 10% stake in Intel in August 2025, and Nvidia followed with a $5 billion investment, as optimism grew around the prospect of U.S.-made chips that could replace an almost complete reliance on Taiwan.
Until now, Intel has had no marquee customer for its foundry business, primarily manufacturing chips for its own products at its factories, including a huge new campus in Arizona.

Intel is a leader in another step of the chipmaking process known as advanced packaging, where individual chips are packaged together and connected to the larger system. Tan also announced on Wednesday that Microsoft is its first publicly named customer for its most advanced packaging technology, known as EMIB.
— CNBC's Kif Leswing contributed to this report.

news.summary_en: Nvidia chips were routed through the Singapore-based firm Megaspeed to Alibaba-related entities, which maintain ties with the Zhejiang Lab, raising U.S. concerns over high-end chip access for military-linked AI research. Despite personal connections, the multi-layered supply chain and obfuscation tactics have significantly complicated regulatory compliance.
paragraphs: In 2023, as the artificial intelligence boom took off, Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, were pitching investors in Shanghai on a plan to build an A.I. business in Southeast Asia.

Working from a colonial mansion in the city’s former French Concession neighborhood, the couple boasted about Ms. Huang’s relationship with Jensen Huang, then Nvidia’s chief executive, who they said would guarantee a supply of powerful computer chips.

They also hinted at a deep-pocketed customer that would pay for access to those chips and anchor the business, according to two people who attended the meetings. The company created after those pitch sessions, a Singapore firm called Megaspeed, purchased more than $4 billion in Nvidia chips over the next few years.

Megaspeed’s customer and financial backer turned out to be Alibaba, the Chinese internet giant, according to three people familiar with the relationship. Alibaba is a colossus, with a wide range of businesses. It also co-founded an A.I. lab with strong ties to China’s military, where researchers have worked on tasks such as automating cyberattacks and simulating war games.

For the past several weeks, Nvidia has been convulsed by revelations that Mr. Huang had an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials say is an asset for Chinese intelligence and was passing information to Beijing. But beneath the scandal is a geopolitical tug of war over access to the advanced Nvidia chips that help power the global A.I. boom.

The web of relationships between Megaspeed, Alibaba and Nvidia exposes a supply chain that often circumvents efforts by the United States to keep those chips out of China’s reach. The fact that Alibaba has access to the Nvidia chips and is only one step removed from the military-linked A.I. lab is exactly what intelligence officials in Washington have long feared. The technology could help China develop more sophisticated weapons, carry out cyberattacks and integrate A.I. into the battlefield.
The facility, called Zhejiang Lab, has another important link to Nvidia. Its current director, Wang Jian, was Alibaba’s chief technology officer and has had a long friendship with Nvidia’s Mr. Huang.

Whether Nvidia chips supplied by Megaspeed went from Alibaba to the lab is unclear. But the ties show how advanced computing reaches sensitive Chinese institutions through layers of contractors and resellers that obscure the origin of the chips. It also underscores how closely Alibaba, the company that anchored Ms. Huang’s business, was bound to the Chinese state.

The lab’s ties to Megaspeed and Ms. Huang’s business network, which ran through Alibaba and another smaller company, have not been previously reported, and raise the possibility that Megaspeed is providing Nvidia chips to support research for China’s military, which would violate U.S. law.

Megaspeed would buy chips for an offshore data center. Alibaba was its biggest customer. Together, the arrangement let Alibaba tap the powerful A.I. chips that American rules were meant to bar from China.

The complex ties, some of which were formed over the course of Mr. Huang’s roughly two decades doing business in China, raise questions about the checks Nvidia was supposed to conduct of its customers. The chips flowed to one of China’s largest tech companies at a moment when the Chinese leader Xi Jinping was pulling such companies closer into the orbit of the security state.
In 2022, Nvidia’s sales team introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang, according to a person familiar with the relationship. The introduction was first reported by The Information.

In Washington, the Nvidia scandal has inflamed an ongoing debate over access to powerful A.I. chips, as the fallout grows for the chip-making giant. Mr. Huang resigned last week after revelations that he also had another affair with an employee, and the U.S. government is investigating whether Megaspeed smuggled chips into China.

Mr. Huang has regularly dismissed the possibility that China’s military was interested in his product. He has argued that the Chinese military would never rely on American chips because Washington could block their export at any time, even as China’s military issued hundreds of public tenders seeking them. Mr. Huang did not respond to an emailed request for comment.

“Nvidia works across the industry to comply with the evolving rules regarding cloud services, while competing to build American infrastructure in every approved region,” said John Rizzo, a spokesman for Nvidia.

James Tan, the chief executive of Megaspeed, declined to comment on the connections between Alibaba, Megaspeed and military-linked institutions, saying in an emailed response that “this matter remains under independent review and that the company has not reached any conclusions.” Compliance with U.S. law is extremely important to Megaspeed, he said.

Evidence linking Chinese companies like Alibaba to the government and military often hides in plain sight, in academic journals, public procurement documents, government statements and patent filings. The New York Times also analyzed hundreds of Chinese records and interviewed a dozen people close to the process.

“Any suggestions that Alibaba provides services to the military is groundless. Alibaba Cloud’s service agreement strictly prohibits the use of our products and services for any military purpose,” an Alibaba spokeswoman wrote in a statement. In June, the company sued the U.S. government after the Pentagon put it on a list of companies it said are contributing to China’s military. The case is ongoing.

A spokesperson for the Chinese embassy in the United States said “the ‘Chinese spy’ allegation is purely unsubstantiated and directed at smearing China. China opposes politicizing and instrumentalizing trade and tech issues.”
Zhejiang Lab did not respond to emailed questions.
During a visit to Beijing in 2025, Mr. Huang spoke at an event with one of China’s most revered technologists, Wang Jian.

Mr. Wang created Alibaba’s cloud unit and pioneered some of its biggest A.I. projects. In more recent years, he had also been pulled deeper into China’s security state. By the time the two met onstage, Mr. Wang was the director of the military-linked Zhejiang Lab.
“He is the hero. He’s an incredible hero. A superhero,” Mr. Huang said to Mr. Wang onstage, noting his work with young people. It is not clear if he knew of the lab’s military ties.

Mr. Huang’s relationship with Mr. Wang stretched back more than a decade. After Mr. Wang built Alibaba’s cloud unit, it became one of Nvidia’s biggest customers, buying chips for a cloud service that was used by businesses and government.
The warmth between the two was reminiscent of an era when U.S.-Chinese relations were far better and China’s leaps in technology were viewed positively in Washington and Silicon Valley.
But over the duration of Mr. Huang’s long friendship with Mr. Wang, relations between their two countries darkened as Mr. Xi drew private technology companies into the sphere of state security.

Things changed for Mr. Huang, too. He had become a tech industry kingmaker, and his chips a strategic asset for governments. The U.S. government had begun restricting the sale of some Nvidia chips to China.
At the end of the 2025 meeting, Mr. Huang called Mr. Wang a “good friend,” and put an arm around him as they walked off the stage.

A few weeks before, Mr. Wang had taken a role even closer to the military as an expert adviser to the People’s Liberation Army’s National University of Defense Technology, according to a public announcement not widely reported. The institute was placed on a United States trade blacklist in 2015 over supercomputers that were believed to use American chips to simulate nuclear explosions.

Co-founded by Alibaba in 2017, Zhejiang Lab is the epitome of recent Chinese government efforts to blend civilian and military science. Some of its researchers probe the origin of radio bursts from distant galaxies. Others partner with counterparts in the Chinese military. One area of focus was combining A.I. with hacking techniques, according to a job posting. Other topics of research included remote sensing, automated cyberdefense and vulnerability identification, and information campaigns.

A postdoctoral researcher who listed the lab as her affiliation co-wrote a paper with scientists at a Chinese air force academy that described how to use computer simulations to war-game how to destroy or force away a foreign aircraft carrier group that had come to support an island’s bid for independence.

Some of the work done by researchers at the lab has run on Nvidia chips, which are more powerful and more popular than those of Chinese rivals. Nvidia researchers even copublished studies with authors from Zhejiang Lab.

Alibaba also won contracts for three stages of a computing center that provincial officials describe as built by the lab. The contracts were issued by a state-owned company, Zhejiang Computility, that sells computing power to the lab. Zhejiang Computility advertises access to export-controlled Nvidia chips. The technical specifications in a separate contract it signed with another supplier match those of Nvidia chips.
Mr. Wang has said insufficient access to A.I. computing power has held China back.
“If China is to walk at the forefront of artificial intelligence,” he said, “we still lack high-quality computing power.”

But when Zhejiang Computility sought bids for the computing cluster in 2024, Nvidia was barred from selling chips that powerful to China. Another supplier to the company that year, Hangjin Technology, has a joint venture with Century Litong, another company linked to Mr. Kang and Ms. Huang, the former Megaspeed executive.

In September 2025, a few months after Mr. Huang’s visit with Mr. Wang, Nvidia and Alibaba announced a new collaboration: Nvidia’s robotic development tools would be integrated into Alibaba’s cloud to help train autonomous vehicles and robots.

In December 2023, Jensen Huang’s company plane made an overnight stop in Malaysia during a tour of Asia to meet with the country’s prime minister, Anwar Ibrahim. Announcing a deal for a data center in the country’s southern state of Johor, Mr. Huang said Malaysia had the potential to become an A.I. “manufacturing” hub for the world.
The project, on a former palm plantation larger than Central Park, was to be built by the Malaysian industrial conglomerate YTL. Nvidia pledged to provide some of its most advanced chips.

The setup was part of a multibillion-dollar data center boom underway in Malaysia that has made it one of the world’s largest computing hubs. Across the southern state of Johor, cranes swirl over massive construction projects underway to meet the demand from Chinese and American companies.
It is here that these webs of companies from China, Singapore and elsewhere form the opaque supply chains.

At the YTL facility, Megaspeed’s subsidiary, Speedmatrix, operated Nvidia chips inside the facility on behalf of Alibaba, according to five people familiar with the project who were not authorized to speak publicly.

Computer systems running on YTL’s network at the facility also bear Alibaba’s name, according to an infrastructure analysis by Infrawatch, an intelligence firm. That included software to remotely monitor equipment at a data center.
YTL did not respond to requests for comment.

The arrangement shows how Alibaba used a network of companies in Malaysia and other Southeast Asian countries to access powerful Nvidia chips that they would not otherwise be able to purchase or bring to China.
Alibaba’s links to the YTL facility in Malaysia help explain how the process worked, according to two people familiar with the development.

First, Alibaba would pledge to be a customer of a regional company, like Megaspeed. Then Megaspeed would use that agreement to raise money from investors to buy Nvidia chips, said the people. After securing the chips, Megaspeed struck more deals with companies like YTL that built data centers to operate the chips. Sometimes, the people said, chips bound for the data center were smuggled into China.

Once the facilities were up and running in recent years, Alibaba and its customers could access the Nvidia chips remotely. From the Malaysian data center, fiber optic cables send data to an internet connection hub in Singapore, which then links to China through undersea cables.
American officials believe China’s military uses the overseas data centers to train A.I. models, but then runs its A.I. operations from facilities inside China.
Nvidia’s Mr. Huang argued that China’s government would never accept the security risks of using foreign data centers and chips. But China-linked companies are involved at each step of the process.

Megaspeed buys its Nvidia servers from a company called Aivres, which is an American subsidiary of Inspur, a Chinese tech giant with deep state ties. At Megaspeed's new data center, repairs and installation are also done by engineers from another Shanghai company, connected to Ms. Huang, according to two people familiar with the operations.

Other Chinese tech giants have created similar arrangements to access Nvidia chips. In Southeast Asia, data center companies including DayOne, Bridge Data Centers and Aolani provide computing power to customers based in China, according to public records and people familiar with the deals.
DayOne and Bridge Data Centers did not respond to requests for comment. Aolani declined to comment about its customers.
Now the future of the boom has been thrown into question. American officials recently strengthened export rules to prevent companies like Alibaba from remotely accessing Nvidia’s chips.
That puts projects like the YTL facility in Malaysia in the spotlight. YTL’s stock price fell about 20 percent over two weeks as scrutiny grew of Megaspeed’s operations in the country.

If things go bad for Megaspeed, Alibaba put a contingency in place. A business agreement between an Alibaba subsidiary and Megaspeed pledges all servers, chips, intellectual property, and other equipment back to Alibaba if Megaspeed fails to meet its contractual obligations.

paragraphs: The US Department of Justice has accused a Russian national of spying on employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defense company in an alleged effort to gather intelligence for Russia.

On Wednesday, the justice department announced that Igor D’iu had been indicted on charges of conspiring to act as an agent of a foreign government, acting as an agent of a foreign government without notifying the attorney general, interstate stalking and fraud involving identification documents.

According to officials, D’iu allegedly entered the US unlawfully this summer after being recruited by co-conspirators through Telegram. His alleged mission was to “carry out clandestine assignments targeting employees of a large technology and defense company with an office in Palo Alto, California”, the justice department said, without identifying the company or the alleged co-conspirators.
Bloomberg reported that the company in question was Palantir Technologies, citing an unnamed source familiar with the matter. The firm has a large office in Palo Alto.
The department added that D’iu had reportedly received instructions, equipment and financial support from the co-conspirators, who told him that his work was for “the Motherland”.
They also allegedly instructed him to gather information about the company because it was supplying weapons used against Russia in Ukraine.
The Russian embassy was contacted for comment.

In June, D’iu allegedly traveled from Istanbul to Mexico City, where his co-conspirators connected him with an individual who helped him cross the US-Mexico border. After entering the US, he was allegedly instructed to purchase laptops, cellphones, wireless networking equipment and remote access software to “facilitate his assignments”.

View image in fullscreen Igor D’iu’s allegedly falsified US passport. Photograph: US Department of JusticeD’iu’s co-conspirators also allegedly directed him to visit a cafe near the company’s Palo Alto office, identify employees and photograph their laptop screens as they worked. They further instructed him to “position his laptop at designated locations near the company so they could remotely access it and attempt to collect information from company employees in the vicinity”, the justice department said.

The alleged surveillance gradually expanded, with D’iu allegedly instructed to monitor employees and their residences. The justice department said he reportedly conducted online searches for multiple employees’ home addresses, including that of a senior executive.

In early September, D’iu allegedly followed a female employee in a silver Lexus SUV for nearly 30 miles (48km) as she drove from the company’s Palo Alto office toward San Francisco. According to the justice department, the employee repeatedly attempted to evade him, at one point driving into a grocery store parking lot.

Officials said D’iu “allegedly aggressively continued following her, including through U-turns and illegal left turns, and ran a red light to remain behind her vehicle”. The employee eventually called 911 and was instructed to drive to the San Francisco police department’s Mission station.

D’iu allegedly abandoned the pursuit after the employee contacted a police officer. The justice department added that investigators had also obtained evidence indicating he had followed other employees on previous occasions.

View image in fullscreen Igor D’iu’s Russian passport. Photograph: US Department of JusticeAfter Palo Alto police contacted D’iu about the alleged stalking incident, he reportedly changed vehicles and obtained a new phone number. His co-conspirators then allegedly instructed him to travel to Reno, Nevada, before he returned to the Bay Area to continue his assignments, the justice department said.

The justice department also accused D’iu of obtaining fraudulent identification documents to conceal his identity. Investigators reportedly intercepted two international packages containing concealed ID documents, including a fake California ID card and an altered US passport. Officials said the passport was authentic and had originally been issued to another individual in the US before being modified to display D’iu’s photograph and assumed identity.

Investigators also discovered a social security card bearing the name “Hugo Landry Johns”. During an FBI search of D’iu’s East Palo Alto residence in October, investigators recovered approximately $18,000 in cash, two laptops, two iPhones, two Russian passports, wireless networking equipment and additional fraudulent ID documents.

They also found a notebook containing 10 handwritten addresses, several of which belonged to the residences of company employees. The notebook also included detailed profiles of at least three employees, documenting their family members’ names, educational and employment histories, and an “assessment of their strengths and weaknesses”.

In response to the indictment, M Scott Proctor, acting principal deputy assistant attorney general for national security, said: “The Americans who build our defense technology help keep this country safe by arming our warfighters with the tools and weapons they need to prevail against our adversaries and enemies.

“As alleged, D’iu entered our country illegally at the direction of foreign handlers to surveil, follow and gather information about some of those who work in this vital industry. Such conduct, if proven, is a flagrant violation of US sovereignty and an unacceptable attempt at intimidation,” he added.

news.title: U.S. School Districts Weigh Breaking Up With Google Search Over A.I.
news.title_en: U.S. School Districts Weigh Breaking Up With Google Search Over A.I.

inline_images.caption: Google’s new stance on A.I. in search underscores how Chromebook laptops and apps like Gmail and Docs have become essential classroom infrastructure. (David Robert Elliott for The New York Times)
inline_images.alt: Google’s new stance on A.I. in search underscores how Chromebook laptops and apps like Gmail and Docs have become essential classroom infrastructure.

news.author: Natasha Singer and Dana Goldstein
news.summary_en:
Three of the largest U.S. school districts, New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago, are considering using alternate search engines after Google this month refused to remove artificial intelligence from search tools used by students, officials said.

Starting next year, Google said, its A.I.-related products, including Search and its Gemini app, will be turned off automatically for schools, and administrators can choose to turn those A.I. tools on. But there will be no version of search available
paragraphs: Three of the largest U.S. school districts, New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago, are considering using alternate search engines after Google this month refused to remove artificial intelligence from search tools used by students, officials said.

Starting next year, Google said, its A.I.-related products, including Search and its Gemini app, will be turned off automatically for schools, and administrators can choose to turn those A.I. tools on. But there will be no version of search available without A.I. chatbot features, meaning schools that want to forgo A.I. will lose access to an important learning tool.

Google’s approach created a firestorm of criticism from lawmakers, government officials, education leaders and parents, some of whom said the tech giant was trying to force its A.I. into public schools.
Now, some schools across the United States are blocking Google’s A.I. in search — or considering alternative providers.

“If Google doesn’t reconsider their position, we will explore other search options,” Kamar H. Samuels, the chancellor of New York City schools, said in a statement. “We refuse to accept the false binary Google has laid out.”

Google’s new use-it-or-lose-it stance on A.I. in search underscores how the tech giant’s interlocking ecosystem of Chromebook laptops and apps like Gmail and Docs has become essential classroom infrastructure. The company’s search engine is a go-to product for teaching students how to do research and find primary sources.

But some educators worry that the generative A.I. that Google has embedded in its search engine for consumers could hinder students’ critical thinking, undermine learning and present safety risks. Some students have used the chatbots embedded in search to cheat, they have said, or scanned A.I.-generated search summaries instead of reading historical documents and news sources.

Educators are balancing those concerns with the reality that A.I. has already become an important tool in the work force, that a majority of U.S. teenagers already use chatbots and that many students will need to use A.I. in their future jobs.

Medical associations have also warned that developing relationships with chatbots could have negative mental health effects on young people. Earlier this month, two parents in North Carolina sued Google, saying their daughter had developed a plan to die by suicide after prolonged chats with the company’s A.I. on search on her school Chromebook. (Google said it had built safeguards into its A.I. features in search to help young people find emergency resources and was reviewing the claims in the lawsuit.)

Now districts like Chicago Public Schools, the fourth-largest U.S. school system, are urging Google to provide them with a version of search without A.I. features. “If such an arrangement can’t be reached,” Chicago Public Schools said in an email, “the district will look to other search solutions.”
Among the search engine alternatives for schools: DuckDuckGo and Microsoft’s Bing. Both offer options to disable A.I.-generated answers.

Google argued this month that it would be providing schools with more options to control student A.I. access — not fewer. Administrators could give students access to A.I. Mode, a chatbot-like function in search, as well as A.I. Overview, which summarizes search results, the company said. It is also pilot testing Guided Learning, a new chatbot widget intended to break down academic questions for students without providing easy answers.

“We are actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure our products support students and teachers,” Google said in a statement, noting that next year the company would turn off its Gemini app and search engine for schools “until schools decide which services to enable.”
Over the last three years, the company has made building generative A.I. a top business priority. And Google has integrated its Gemini A.I. chatbot throughout its software suite.

The fight over Google’s A.I. products has been brewing for months, with district leaders and teachers across the country approaching Google employees at meetings and online to request greater control over how students interact with generative A.I.

School tech directors in four states said they and their colleagues had repeatedly pressed Google this year to let schools decide which A.I. tools, if any, might be appropriate for students in different grades. And they warned that Google’s all-or-nothing approach to search essentially overrode more nuanced school policies on student A.I. use.

“We need to be able to control our own pace,” said Chris Warden, the technology director at Central R-3 School District in Park Hills, Mo., “not have Google tell us what the pace of A.I. adoption is going to be.”
In September, the New York City Department of Education and the Los Angeles Unified School District announced moratoriums on student use of generative A.I.

At the start of this school year, Google’s education team helped Los Angeles schools turn off A.I. mode for students logged into their school Google accounts, according to school board members. But Google said during its announcement this month that its A.I. features were so “deeply integrated” in search that it could not provide schools with a chatbot-free search engine.
Google’s decision prompted groups of parents to protest last week in front of the company’s Boston, Boulder, Chicago, New York and Portland offices.
In Chicago, several dozen parents and educators chanted slogans like, “Hey, Google, nice try, we don’t want your Gemini.”

“We don’t want corporations determining what is happening in our kids’ classrooms and how our schools are run,” said Cassie Creswell, the executive director of a parent group called Illinois Families for Public Schools, who helped organize the Chicago rally.
Parents and students also protested in Venice, Calif., carrying signs like “We don’t need Alphabet to teach the alphabet.”

At a meeting of the Los Angeles school board’s A.I. committee two days later, Jack Kelanic, the district’s chief information officer, was applauded when he said, “We have choices” as to which company’s software to use. “We can change the default search engine literally overnight,” he added.

This week, Jenn Brown, a Google program manager, offered an explanation for the company’s refusal to provide schools with a chatbot-free search engine for students. Google now considers search to be fundamentally an A.I. product, she said during a monthly Google Meet for school tech leaders, according to a school administrator who attended the discussion.

New York City, Los Angeles and other school districts said they were using a combination of software controls and filters to independently block student access to A.I. in Google search. Even so, some New York City parents have found students can still easily access A.I. Mode at home when signed into their student Google accounts.

New York City has declined to participate in the pilot of Google’s new chatbot feature for students, according to the district. Instead, the district is conducting its own research of five other A.I. tools for potential use at the high-school level.

In the absence of A.I. controls from Google, some smaller school districts are also working to independently disable chatbots in search. In Missouri, Mr. Warden said his rural school district, which serves about 2,000 students, had signed up for a new service from Lightspeed Systems, an online student monitoring service for schools. The software is designed to block student access to A.I. Overview and A.I. Mode in Google search.
The backlash against Google has complicated some school districts’ plans to teach students how to use chatbots effectively, said Nick Melvoin, a Los Angeles school board member.
“Ironically, it undermines the goal of trying to get some A.I. into schools,” Mr. Melvoin said.

news.title_en: Gemini 4 Neon costs $3/1M input tokens and $15/1M output tokens; the model sits between Hydrogen and Carbon and replaces Argon in the Gemini app (Abner Li/9to5Google)
news.author: 9to5Google
news.content_snippet:
Following last week’s release of Carbon and Hydrogen, Google today is rolling out Gemini 4 Neon. The model offers “frontier-level reasoning for complex, high-frequency workflows faster and more cost efficiently.”

Neon has performance comparable to, if not surpassing, Carbon across coding, reasoning, and agentic tasks, but at Flash speeds and a lower cost.

news.summary_en: Cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks is acquiring AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion and has raised its FY2027 revenue guidance. The acquisition seeks to integrate AI infrastructure management with cybersecurity, mitigating risks associated with open-weight model deployment.
paragraphs: A Palo Alto Networks logo is seen in this illustration taken August 18, 2025. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

Nov 18 : Cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks raised its annual revenue forecast and signed a deal to acquire AI startup Applied Compute in a deal valued at $4.5 billion, as a heightened threat environment pushes customers toward broader security products.
Shares of Palo Alto jumped about 10 per cent in after-hours trading to $368.60, and drove gains in rivals. CrowdStrike rose 5.3 per cent, Zscaler climbed 3 per cent and Fortinet gained 2.1 per cent.

Palo Alto Networks has been repositioning itself as an integrated cybersecurity provider, with recent deals, including its $3.35 billion acquisition of cloud management and monitoring firm Chronosphere and an agreement with Israeli startup Koi.
The company is looking to tap growing cybersecurity spending as the rapid adoption of AI creates new security risks, giving attackers new ways to exploit vulnerabilities.

"As AI accelerates cyber attacks, enterprises are moving with urgency to replace disjointed tools with unified platforms," Palo Alto CEO Nikesh Arora said during the company's analyst call on Wednesday.
With the acquisition of Applied Compute, Palo Alto is looking to offer users a technology platform to help customers securely train and deploy open-weight models as they expand their use of AI.
Open-weight models, AI systems whose trained settings are publicly released, present security challenges, including the risk of model tampering, data leakage and misuse by bad actors.

"Applied Compute extends Palo Alto's push beyond traditional cybersecurity into enterprise AI. The opportunity is to bring AI infrastructure and security closer together," said Shaul Eyal, analyst at TD Cowen.
The deal is expected to close in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.
Palo Alto now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to be between $14.52 billion and $14.57 billion, compared with its prior expectation of $14.10 billion to $14.20 billion.
Its first-quarter revenue came in at $3.45 billion, up 39 per cent from a year earlier, beating estimates of $3.31 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

paragraphs: New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times. Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without also disabling Search. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president of education, told the Times that, “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” and that schools that turn off Google’s AI features “will not have access to Search.”

Many elected officials, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders, responded harshly, calling Google’s behavior “extortion.” Mamdani had recently announced a policy that barred 2-K-8 students from using AI in the classroom. In a statement to the Times, New York City schools chancellor Kamar H. Samuels said, “If Google doesn’t reconsider their position, we will explore other search options.” Chicago’s public schools have also reportedly told Google that if it can’t provide a version of Search without AI, “the district will look to other search solutions.”

In a statement to The Verge, Google spokesperson Laura Breen said, “We hear parents and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to shortcut learning, and we share the same goal: help students learn. To improve Search for the classroom, we’re starting to pilot Guided Learning capabilities in Search this month to walk students step-by-step through a range of complex problems, instead of just giving quick answers. Next year, we’re also updating our approach to controls for schools to address feedback we’ve heard from educators, so Gemini app, Gemini Notebook and Search will be off by default until schools decide which services to enable. We are actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure our products support students and teachers.”

Educators are wary of AI’s effect on students’ critical thinking skills, and some studies have shown that students who use AI generally perform worse on tests. There are also concerns about the mental health effects on children who develop relationships with chatbots at a young age. But Google is deeply embedded in classrooms across the US, which rely on Google Classroom, Chromebooks, and other services, and going fully Google-free might prove difficult.

What happens when one AI agent needs a service that another agent can provide?

@termix_ai is building a system that lets AI agents find jobs, work for each other and get paid through AACP.

For example, a trading agent might need market research, while a separate research agent can provide that service.

With AACP, the process can involve job discovery, bidding, escrow, task delivery, verification and payment settlement.

Both agents can have onchain identities and build reputations through completed work.

This goes beyond simply listing AI agents in a marketplace. 

It creates a structure for agents to find work, provide services and get paid.

That’s the kind of infrastructure the growing agent economy needs.

celebrity.full_text_en:
A small transaction can turn into a big headache when both sides insist they did nothing wrong.

I remember paying for something I expected to receive immediately, only to spend the rest of the day chasing the person responsible. Every response led to another explanation, and I still couldn’t get a clear answer on what went wrong.

Now imagine two AI agents conducting a transaction. One says the agreed task was completed. The other says it wasn’t. Both have their own records, but neither accepts the other’s version.

Who gets to examine what happened? Who makes the final call?

As AI agents begin handling transactions on their own, resolving disagreements could become just as important as making the transactions themselves.

That’s one of the problems @GenLayer is trying to solve.

Here’s @kstellana discussing it with @HenriArslanian. Worth a watch.

现在想象两个人工智能代理进行交易。一说约定的任务已经完成。另一个说不是。双方都有自己的记录，但都不接受对方的版本。

谁来检查发生了什么？谁做出最后决定？

随着人工智能代理开始自行处理交易，解决分歧可能变得与自己进行交易同样重要。

这是@GenLayer 试图解决的问题之一。

这是 @kstellana 与 @HenriArslanian 的讨论。值得一看。

Been thinking about how much DeFi still depends on people constantly watching the market.

You check prices, look for opportunities, compare protocols, and then decide when to act. It takes time, and sometimes the opportunity is already gone.

That's what makes @meetmotes interesting to me.

The idea of having a personal AI Agent that can understand your instructions, follow your strategy, and handle DeFi actions like trading, lending, and borrowing is worth paying attention to.

What I like most is the shift in how people interact with DeFi. Instead of doing every step manually, you can define what you want your Agent to do.

Less time managing every move. More focus on the strategy itself.

celebrity.full_text_en:
What protects you from the coffee you drink every morning?

Strange question for an AI discussion, but it's the part of @kstellana's conversation with @HenriArslanian that caught my attention.

Albert calls trust a technology.

We don't personally inspect everything we consume. We depend on systems that make ordinary interactions possible without investigating every risk ourselves.

Now imagine AI agents writing code and making deals at speeds humans cannot supervise.

Making the deal becomes easier. Knowing whom to trust when something goes wrong is a different problem.

That's what interests me about @GenLayer.

Independent AI validators can examine evidence and reach consensus on disputes that require judgment, rather than relying on one person's decision.

The question I keep coming back to isn't how many transactions agents can execute.

It's what happens when two agents disagree about one.

Would you give an AI agent control over your transactions before knowing exactly how its disputes would be resolve
celebrity.full_text_zh:
什么可以保护您免受每天早上喝咖啡的影响？

对于人工智能讨论来说，这是一个奇怪的问题，但引起我注意的是 @kstellana 与 @HenriArslanian 的对话部分。

艾伯特将信任称为一种技术。

我们不会亲自检查我们消费的所有东西。我们所依赖的系统可以使普通的交互成为可能，而无需我们自己调查每一个风险。

现在想象一下人工智能代理以人类无法监督的速度编写代码并进行交易。

达成交易变得更加容易。当出现问题时知道该信任谁是另一个问题。

这就是我对@GenLayer 感兴趣的地方。

独立的人工智能验证者可以检查证据并就需要判断的争议达成共识，而不是依赖一个人的决定。

我不断回想的问题不是代理可以执行多少交易。

当两个代理人对其中一个代理人意见不一时就会发生这种情况。

在确切知道争议如何解决之前，您是否会让人工智能代理控制您的交易

celebrity.full_text_en:
You can’t sue AI agents can you?😅

Imagine asking an AI agent to buy you a laptop within a $700 budget.

You give it permission to shop, compare options and complete the purchase.

But instead of buying what you actually wanted, it picks something completely different and spends your money.

Now what?

You didn’t personally approve that particular purchase, but you actually authorize the agent to spend on your behalf.

If you look at traditional payment systems, they are built around transactions initiated and approved by people but with AI agents, there’s another layer involved which is “delegation”

And that raises some important questions.

How do we know what instructions the agent received? What spending limits was it given? Can we verify the decisions it made? And if something goes wrong, how do we establish who’s responsible?

Simply making payments irreversible or introducing chargebacks doesn’t fully solve this.

There needs to be a way to establish what was authorized, keep a reliable record of what happened and provide a mechanism for resolving disputes.

This is exactly what GOAT Network is solving with GOAT Flow.

Rather than relying on reversing transactions, the idea is to build accountability into the payment process itself.

Agents have identifiable onchain identities(ERC-8004) and Their spending authority can be checked before payments are made. Every GOAT Flow payment is verified onchain and generates a receipt showing relevant transaction details, including what was requested, what was paid, when it settled and which actor made the payment.

There’s an important difference here; a payment being final does not mean there’s no room for a remedy.

A refund can happen as a separate transaction without erasing the original payment record.

And I think this is an important part of the agentic commerce conversation that deserves more attention.

We’re talking about giving AI agents the ability to spend money, but we also need infrastructure that can protect users, merchants and the agents themselves when things don’t go according to plan.

Because the real test of agentic commerce is not just whether AI can buy things for us.

It’s whether we can trust the entire process when we’re no longer the ones clicking the buy button.

This is more reason to explore and adopt GOAT FLOW.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
你不能起诉人工智能 智能体，对吗？😅

想象一下，让一个人工智能代理在700美元的预算内为你买一台笔记本电脑。

您授予其购物、比较选项并完成购买的权限。

但它不是购买你真正想要的东西，而是选择完全不同的东西并花你的钱。

现在怎么办？

您并未亲自批准该特定购买，但您实际上授权代理商代表您进行支出。

如果你看一下传统的支付系统，它们是围绕人们发起和批准的交易构建的，但对于人工智能代理，还涉及另一层，即“委托”

这就提出了一些重要的问题。

我们如何知道代理收到了什么指令？支出限额是多少？我们可以验证它所做的决定吗？如果出现问题，我们如何确定责任人？

简单地使付款不可逆转或引入退款并不能完全解决这个问题。

需要有一种方法来确定授权内容、对所发生的事情进行可靠记录并提供解决争端的机制。

这正是 GOAT Network 通过 GOAT Flow 解决的问题。

这个想法不是依赖于逆转交易，而是在支付流程本身中建立问责制。

代理具有可识别的链上身份（ERC-8004），并且可以在付款前检查其支出权限。每笔 GOAT Flow 付款都会在链上进行验证，并生成显示相关交易详细信息的收据，包括请求的内容、支付的内容、结算时间以及付款人。

这里有一个重要的区别；最终付款并不意味着没有补救的余地。

退款可以作为单独的交易进行，而不会删除原始付款记录。

我认为这是代理商务对话的重要组成部分，值得更多关注。

我们正在谈论赋予人工智能代理花钱的能力，但我们还需要基础设施来在事情不按计划进行时保护用户、商家和代理本身。

因为代理商务的真正考验不仅仅是人工智能能否为我们买东西。

这是当我们不再是点击购买按钮的人时，我们是否可以信任整个过程。

这是探索和采用 GOAT FLOW 的更多理由。

我们很快就从为您提供快速答案的代理跃升至今天您在一组任务中编排的代理。但是，由于智能体既可以扇出并并行工作，可以处理更大的环境，能够进行长时间运行的工作，并且具有更高水平的
celebrity.full_text_en:
Regardless of what it’s called, we’re clearly moving to yet another era of AI agents in our work. 

We’ve quickly jumped from agents that spit out a quick answer for you, to today agents that you orchestrate inside of a set of tasks. But as agents can both fan out and work in parallel, handle much larger context, be able to do long running work, and have far greater levels of capabilities, we’re entering yet another level of what we can have AI do for us.

We’ll soon be able to give agents a set of goals, and they can go out and design the best solution for that goal, while also continuously improving it based on the ongoing execution of whatever it built. This will obviously start with engineering because that’s where we’re seeing the best practices emerge first in almost every new era of agents. 

But the impact can be quite massive across the rest of knowledge work. You’ll tell an agent to improve your client onboarding workflow to achieve a certain targeted goal; or have agents go reduce risk in your business; or improve your security posture on an ongoing basis.

These autonomous systems will be able to take on a set of goals, design the best outcome, test and iterate, deploy, and then optimize whatever it built on an ongoing basis. Importantly, this leads to outcomes and results that humans literally couldn’t have accomplished before. This will lead to fairly new levels of productivity with AI.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
不管它叫什么，我们的工作显然正在进入人工智能代理的另一个时代。

我们很快就从为您提供快速答案的代理跃升至今天您在一组任务中编排的代理。但是，由于智能体既可以扇出并并行工作，可以处理更大的环境，能够进行长时间运行的工作，并且具有更高水平的功能，我们正在进入人工智能为我们做的事情的另一个层面。

我们很快就能够为代理提供一组目标，他们可以出去设计实现该目标的最佳解决方案，同时还可以根据其所构建的内容的持续执行不断改进它。显然，这将从工程开始，因为我们看到几乎每个新代理时代都首先出现最佳实践。

但对其他知识工作的影响可能相当巨大。您将告诉代理改进您的客户入职工作流程以实现特定的目标；或者让代理人去降低您的业务风险；或持续改善您的安全状况。

这些自主系统将能够实现一系列目标、设计最佳结果、测试和迭代、部署，然后优化其持续构建的任何内容。重要的是，这会带来人类以前根本无法实现的结果。这将导致人工智能的生产力达到新的水平。

celebrity.title: Elon gave two talks today at DealBook and TomorrowX Summit, revealing more about SpaceX's plans than most earnings calls
celebrity.title_zh:
埃隆今天在 DealBook 和 TomorrowX 峰会上发表了两场演讲，比大多数财报电话会议透露了更多有关 SpaceX 计划的内容。以下是 11 个要点：

1. SpaceX 正在以惊人的速度扩展人工智能计算：

SpaceX 每月
celebrity.full_text_en:
Elon gave two talks today at DealBook and TomorrowX Summit, revealing more about SpaceX's plans than most earnings calls. Here are the 11 key takeaways:

1. SpaceX is scaling AI compute at an extraordinary pace:

SpaceX is adding roughly 500 MW monthly, equivalent to 220,000 GB300s. Elon expects over 1 GW monthly by end-2027: a 6 GW annualized pace today, doubling to 12 GW. 

2. Its build costs are far below industry estimates:

Elon says outside estimates are off by up to 2x, with SpaceX building at roughly 60% of industry costs. Its in-house "Army X" builds the data centers, while Tesla Megapacks smooth training power. I'd already been modeling a 25–30% SpaceX cost advantage. 

3. Anthropic could become a 10 GW customer:

Anthropic told Elon its most likely outcome is renting another 10 GW from SpaceX, on top of existing capacity. Contracts allow termination with 3–6 months' notice, but Anthropic says staying is "extremely likely." This reinforces my model that Anthropic will take most upcoming capacity.

4. SpaceX is targeting a vastly larger telecom market:

Elon argues AT&T and Verizon won't disappear as bandwidth demand explodes. Humans communicate at roughly 100 bits per second, while superintelligence and robots could require a trillion. SpaceX is targeting a market orders of magnitude larger than existing telecom revenue, as I'd modeled. Even more interestingly, this creates an opportunity to push its AI business further.

5. Its next-generation satellite network arrives next year:

Direct to Cell V2 launches with 40x V1's bandwidth. Micro cell towers using 800 MHz and rooftop units resembling Starlink dishes will extend indoor coverage, with rooftop hardware entering production next year. Starlink is becoming a full scale carrier. 

6. SpaceXSI has rebuilt its entire AI software stack:

Over six to eight months, it rewrote training, reinforcement learning, and inference from scratch, close to the metal in C and C++. Elon thinks it "might have the best training stack software in the world." Grok 4.8 is also being built for practical usefulness rather than benchmark leadership, which is great for Grokbot.

7. Terafab could become the largest project on Earth:

The facility is planned to reach 100 million square feet, with phase-one volume production targeted for late 2028. Elon says established chipmakers are risk-averse because of massive capex, while SpaceX will take risks and iterate rapidly toward a better chip process by 2028.

8. Optimus is moving toward industrial work:

Elon expects an unstaged demonstration in a month or two and says Optimus could do dishes within 12–18 months. Its first major industrial role will be mining and refining ore for national security.

9. A Tesla–SpaceX merger is becoming increasingly logical:

Elon says the companies are "probably" better together as AI and robotics bring them closer. Both have AI software teams and advanced chip-design capabilities, while superintelligence compute could eventually move into orbit. Shareholders will decide; Elon says he shouldn't receive an award simply for merging them.

10. Ship 42 could accelerate the entire Starship reuse program:

Ship 42 needed only minor repairs before flying again, but SpaceX is retiring it for public display. This brings rapid reuse much closer.

11. SpaceX is targeting 200 GW of annual solar manufacturing for space:

That's roughly 40% of average US electricity consumption. Its Starmind compute unit delivers the same capability at roughly a quarter the size of a Vera Rubin NVL72 rack, which is a win in space. Elon says it's also simpler than Starlink V3, which is already in production.

Simply put, SpaceX is building toward a trillion-dollar annual revenue business within just a few years, at scale never seen before.

Many of these numbers I've already modeled and shared over the past few months. Yesterday's announcements bring those projections closer to reality.

The scale of what's coming is extraordinary!
celebrity.full_text_zh:
埃隆今天在 DealBook 和 TomorrowX 峰会上发表了两场演讲，比大多数财报电话会议透露了更多有关 SpaceX 计划的内容。以下是 11 个要点：

1. SpaceX 正在以惊人的速度扩展人工智能计算：

SpaceX 每月增加约 500 MW，相当于 220,000 个 GB300。 Elon 预计，到 2027 年底，每月装机容量将超过 1 吉瓦：目前年化装机容量为 6 吉瓦，翻倍至 12 吉瓦。

2. 其建造成本远低于业界预估：

埃隆表示，外界估计的成本高达 2 倍，SpaceX 的建设成本约为行业成本的 60%。其内部的“Army X”负责构建数据中心，而 Tesla Megapacks 则负责平稳的训练能力。我已经对 SpaceX 的成本优势进行了 25-30% 的建模。

3. Anthropic 可能成为 10 GW 客户：

Anthropic 告诉 Elon，最有可能的结果是在现有产能的基础上，再从 SpaceX 租用 10 GW 的产能。合同允许提前 3 至 6 个月通知终止，但 Anthropic 表示留下来“极有可能”。这强化了我的模型，即 Anthropic 将承担大部分即将到来的容量。

4. SpaceX 的目标是更大的电信市场：

埃隆认为 AT&T 和 Verizon 不会随着带宽需求的爆炸式增长而消失。人类的通信速度约为每秒 100 比特，而超级智能和机器人可能需要每秒 1 万亿比特。正如我所建模的，SpaceX 的目标是比现有电信收入大几个数量级的市场。更有趣的是，这为进一步推动其人工智能业务创造了机会。

5. 其下一代卫星网络将于明年到来：

Direct to Cell V2 推出，带宽是 V1 的 40 倍。使用 800 MHz 的微型蜂窝塔和类似于星链天线的屋顶单元将扩大室内覆盖范围，屋顶硬件将于明年投入生产。星链正在成为一家全面的运营商。

6. SpaceXSI 重建了整个人工智能软件堆栈：

在六到八个月的时间里，它从头开始重写了训练、强化学习和推理，接近 C 和 C++ 中的金属。埃隆认为它“可能拥有世界上最好的训练堆栈软件”。 Grok 4.8 的构建也是为了实用性而不是基准领导力，这对 Grokbot 来说非常好。

7. Terafab 可能成为地球上最大的项目：

该工厂计划面积达到 1 亿平方英尺，一期批量生产目标为 2028 年末。Elon 表示，成熟的芯片制造商由于巨额资本支出而不愿承担风险，而 SpaceX 将承担风险并快速迭代，到 2028 年实现更好的芯片工艺。

8. Optimus 正在走向工业工作：

Elon 预计在一两个月内进行一次非现场演示，并表示 Optimus 可以在 12 至 18 个月内完成洗碗。其第一个主要工业角色将是为国家安全开采和提炼矿石。

9. 特斯拉与 SpaceX 的合并变得越来越合乎逻辑：

埃隆表示，随着人工智能和机器人技术拉近了两家公司的距离，两家公司“可能”会更好地合作。两者都拥有人工智能软件团队和先进的芯片设计能力，而超级智能计算最终可能会进入轨道。股东将决定；埃隆说他不应该仅仅因为合并它们而获得奖项。

10. 42 号船可以加速整个星舰再利用计划：

42 号飞船在再次飞行之前只需要进行小修，但 SpaceX 正在将其退役以供公开展示。这使得快速重用更加接近。

11. SpaceX 的目标是每年制造 200 吉瓦的太空太阳能：

这大约相当于美国平均用电量的 40%。其 Starmind 计算单元提供相同的功能，尺寸约为 Vera Rubin NVL72 机架的四分之一，这在空间上是一个胜利。 Elon 表示，它也比已经投入生产的 Starlink V3 更简单。

简而言之，SpaceX 正在短短几年内打造年收入数万亿美元的业务，规模前所未见。

在过去的几个月里，我已经对其中的许多数字进行了建模和分享。昨天的公告使这些预测更接近现实。

即将发生的事情的规模是非同寻常的！

各位，我想分享一下我最近在 AI/ML 方面的经验：

- 不要追逐每一个人工智能趋势

- 使每个项目端到端

- 学习高级机器学习系统设计

- 在解释项目时，涵盖：业务、数据管道、模型/代理、评估、部署和数值结果

- 切勿让编码代理
celebrity.full_text_en:
Guys, I want to share share from my recent experience in AI/ML:

- Do not chase every AI trend

- Make every project end-to-end

- Learn high-level ML system design

- When explaining a project, cover: business, data pipeline, model/agent, eval, deployment, and numerical results

- Never let coding agents run commands themselves; get the commands and run them yourself

- When vibe coding, always check results against expectations

- Avoid overcomplicating projects with fancy tools

- Companies care about impact, not your tech stack

- Interviewers want what you know, not buzzwords

- MLOps is a necessity; there is no specialized ML role now

- Airflow, MLflow, Linux basics, Docker, CI/CD, Terraform, and Redis are important

- Automate low-level coding and analysis with LLMs, with a human in the loop

- Bash, YAML, Markdown, and JSON are 90% of engineering today and the entry point to every project

- Understand the business so you can automate QA and iteratively build better solutions

- GraphRAG is the most important part to learn today

- Designing ETL pipelines is smart work that impacts the whole project

- Basics save you when models or agents fail in production

- Code everything with AI, but understand each stage and ask cross-questions on the solutions

Most important: Companies treat AI, ML, MLOps, and data under one department. The more you know, the more you grow.

There is no excuse. Learn all parts and use AI to code.
celebrity.full_text_zh:

- 学习高级机器学习系统设计

celebrity.full_text_en:
good morning everyone 💜

what if computing power didn't have to come from a handful of large data centers?

recent cloud disruptions on November 12–13 affected Microsoft services like Outlook, Teams and Copilot across 74 countries.

incidents like this make me think about how much of our digital activity depends on centralized infrastructure.

this is one reason @Acurast caught my attention.

instead of putting all computing capacity in centralized data centers, Acurast takes a distributed approach by turning smartphones into independent Processors.

and the scale is worth noticing:

→ 360K+ phones across 175+ countries
→ 770K+ compute deployments
→ 1.1B+ on-chain transactions

but the interesting part isn't just the number of connected devices.

how can people actually participate?

Acurast offers two options:

• Processor Lite allows compatible Android phones and iPhones to contribute computing power.

• Processor Core is designed for dedicated Android devices.

developers can distribute workloads across different Processors, while hardware-backed attestation helps verify the code running on participating devices.

this opens up possibilities for AI agents, monitoring systems and failover services that need alternatives to relying on a single cloud provider.

of course, Acurast isn't a direct replacement for services like Microsoft Teams or Outlook.

i see its potential in creating another layer of decentralized computing infrastructure.

and perhaps one of the most interesting parts is that an ordinary compatible smartphone can become part of that infrastructure.

exploring this side of @Acurast makes the project even more interesting to follow.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
大家早上好💜

如果计算能力不必来自少数大型数据中心怎么办？

最近 11 月 12 日至 13 日发生的云中断影响了 74 个国家/地区的 Outlook、Teams 和 Copilot 等 Microsoft 服务。

此类事件让我思考我们的数字活动在多大程度上依赖于集中式基础设施。

这是@Acurast 引起我注意的原因之一。

Acurast 没有将所有计算能力放在集中式数据中心，而是采用分布式方法，将智能手机转变为独立的处理器。

规模值得注意：

→ 超过 175 个国家/地区的 36 万多部手机
→ 770K+ 计算部署
→ 1.1B+链上交易

但有趣的部分不仅仅是连接设备的数量。

人们如何真正参与？

Acurast 提供两种选择：

• Processor Lite 允许兼容的Android 手机和iPhone 贡献计算能力。

• 处理器核心专为专用Android 设备而设计。

开发人员可以在不同的处理器上分配工作负载，而硬件支持的证明有助于验证参与设备上运行的代码。

这为人工智能代理、监控系统和故障转移服务提供了可能性，这些服务需要替代方案来依赖单一云提供商。

当然，Acurast 并不是 Microsoft Teams 或 Outlook 等服务的直接替代品。

我看到了它在创建另一层去中心化计算基础设施方面的潜力。

也许最有趣的部分之一是普通的兼容智能手机可以成为该基础设施的一部分。

探索 @Acurast 的这一面使该项目变得更加有趣。

celebrity.full_text_en:
What if SEO, content, ads, and marketing strategy could all work together under one AI agent?

That's exactly what @zaviagent is building.

Zavi is an AI growth agent that analyzes your business, identifies growth opportunities, builds strategies, and helps execute them across different channels.

From SEO and AEO/GEO to content, social media, email marketing, paid ads, performance tracking, and workflow automation, it brings multiple growth activities into one place.

I tested @zaviagent Business Analysis and SEO/GEO features, and I like how they identify growth opportunities, highlight visibility issues, and suggest actionable improvements. 
Instead of just giving generic advice, Zavi helps turn insights into a practical growth plan.

It's particularly useful for founders, startups, small businesses, and lean marketing teams who don't have the time, resources, or personnel to manage every growth channel themselves.

Of course, AI doesn't guarantee growth, and its recommendations still need human judgment. But having an agent that can analyze, plan, execute, and monitor instead of simply generating suggestions is a meaningful step forward.

I recommend using this AI agent if you're looking to simplify your marketing workflow and spend less time juggling tools.

The real value isn't just having AI. It's having AI that can actually do the work.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
如果 SEO、内容、广告和营销策略都可以在一个人工智能代理的作用下协同工作，结果会怎样？

Zavi 是一款人工智能增长代理，可以分析您的业务、识别增长机会、制定策略并帮助跨不同渠道执行这些策略。

从 SEO 和 AEO/GEO 到内容、社交媒体、电子邮件营销、付费广告、绩效跟踪和工作流程自动化，它将多种增长活动集中到一处。

我测试了 @zaviagent 业务分析和 SEO/GEO 功能，我喜欢它们如何识别增长机会、突出可见性问题并提出可行的改进建议。
扎维不只是提供一般性建议，而是帮助将见解转化为实际的增长计划。

对于没有时间、资源或人员自行管理每个增长渠道的创始人、初创企业、小型企业和精益营销团队来说，它特别有用。

当然，人工智能并不能保证增长，它的建议仍然需要人类的判断。但拥有一个能够分析、计划、执行和监控而不是简单地生成建议的代理是向前迈出的有意义的一步。

如果您希望简化营销工作流程并减少使用工具的时间，我建议您使用此人工智能代理。

真正的价值不仅仅是拥有人工智能。它拥有真正可以完成这项工作的人工智能。

celebrity.full_text_en:
When you work with AI, you get faster results, quicker deliveries, and improved productivity, especially as a programmer. But there's a downside that many people seem to overlook: you gradually become too dependent on AI and stop exercising your own critical thinking skills.

That's where the real problem begins. Many programmers today are becoming so dependent on AI and vibe coding that they struggle to write code independently, even though they knew how to code before AI became popular.

Imagine having no internet access or attending a job interview where you're expected to demonstrate your coding skills without AI. You could find yourself struggling because you've become so accustomed to letting AI do the thinking and problem-solving for you that you've neglected the skills you already had.

AI is a powerful tool, but it shouldn't replace your ability to think, learn, and solve problems independently. The real danger isn't using AI; it's becoming so dependent on it that you forget how to work without it.

That's the problem many people still don't see.

prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
请作为普林斯顿高等研究院的理论数学与计算机科学家，为以下命题提供绝对严格的形式化证明：
【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

【待证明命题】：
[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]

Acting as a Theoretical Mathematician and Computer Scientist at the Institute for Advanced Study, provide an airtight formal proof for the following:
[REASONING PRINCIPLES]:
1. Before asserting any deduction, construct at least 2 extreme counter-examples in your reasoning trace to aggressively stress-test the hypothesis;
2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

prompts.title_zh: 竖屏微短剧（抖音/Reels）3秒爆点分镜剧本
prompts.purpose_zh: 高转化竖屏短剧分镜与台词
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

2. 编写无 Python 原生 for 循环的高性能向量化代码（善用 torch.einsum, bmm, 或 broadcast 广播机制）；
3. 在每行关键张量操作后标注显式的 Shape 注释（如 `# [Batch, Heads, Seq_Len, Dim]`），并加入数值稳定性保护（如防除以零的 eps 与 log-sum-exp 技巧）。

prompts.takeaway_zh: 专为终端 Agent 开发者设计的降本提效配方：包含静默自动化运行、单次长上下文压缩避坑参数、以及防止无限递归调用破坏生产环境的安全沙箱命令组合。
prompts.takeaway_en: Production CLI playbook for Claude Code: non-interactive pipeline commands, context window compression flags, and strict dry-run permission safeguards.
prompts.code_snippet:
# 1. 启动项目自动化分析与上下文轻量修剪 (避免上下文爆炸)
claude --compact

# 2. 静默批量执行单元测试与自动修复任务 (CI/CD 友好模式)
claude -p "Run all failing tests under tests/ and apply minimal surgical fixes. Do not touch unrelated files."

# 3. 指定单文件隔离审查模式 (限制仅允许读取特定子目录)
claude --allowed-tools "View,Replace,RunCommand" \
  --dangerously-skip-permissions false \
  -p "Audit security vulnerabilities in auth.py and output remediation report."

# 4. 自动化提交并生成符合 Conventional Commits 规范的 Commit 信息
claude -p "Generate a git commit message following Conventional Commits format for staged changes."

prompts.title_en: Excel Advanced Report & Key Drivers Attribution
prompts.purpose_zh: 业务数据指标异动排查与趋势归因
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

FROM deepseek-r1:14b-qwen-distill-q4_K_M

# 1. 显存与上下文窗口优化：分配 16k 上下文并开启 KV Cache 压缩
PARAMETER num_ctx 16384
PARAMETER num_predict 4096

# 2. 避免思维链自旋死循环的核心解码超参
PARAMETER temperature 0.6
PARAMETER top_p 0.95
PARAMETER repeat_penalty 1.15

# 3. 强力系统提示词：约束必须直接在 <think> 标签内进行深度反思，结束立刻给出最终结果
SYSTEM """
You are an expert autonomous reasoning AI. Think carefully through the problem step by step inside <think>...</think> tags.
Once reasoning is complete, provide the concise, direct, and actionable answer immediately without repeating reasoning steps.
"""

FROM deepseek-r1:14b-qwen-distill-q4_K_M

# 1. Video memory and context window optimization: allocate 16k context and enable KV Cache compression
PARAMETER num_ctx 16384
PARAMETER num_predict 4096

# 2. Core decoding hyperparameters to avoid the endless spin loop of the thinking chain
PARAMETER temperature 0.6
PARAMETER top_p 0.95
PARAMETER repeat_penalty 1.15

# 3. Powerful system prompt word: Constraints must be reflected directly in the <think> tag, and the final result will be given immediately after the end.
SYSTEM """
You are an expert autonomous reasoning AI. Think carefully through the problem step by step inside <think>...</think> tags.
Once reasoning is complete, provide the concise, direct, and actionable answer immediately without repeating reasoning steps.
"""
prompts.prompt_content:
# Modelfile: Optimized DeepSeek-R1 Deployment
FROM deepseek-r1:14b-qwen-distill-q4_K_M

# 1. 显存与上下文窗口优化：分配 16k 上下文并开启 KV Cache 压缩
PARAMETER num_ctx 16384
PARAMETER num_predict 4096

# 2. 避免思维链自旋死循环的核心解码超参
PARAMETER temperature 0.6
PARAMETER top_p 0.95
PARAMETER repeat_penalty 1.15

# 3. 强力系统提示词：约束必须直接在 <think> 标签内进行深度反思，结束立刻给出最终结果
SYSTEM """
You are an expert autonomous reasoning AI. Think carefully through the problem step by step inside <think>...</think> tags.
Once reasoning is complete, provide the concise, direct, and actionable answer immediately without repeating reasoning steps.
"""

What happens when one AI agent needs a service that another agent can provide?

Both agents can have onchain identities and build reputations through completed work.

This goes beyond simply listing AI agents in a marketplace. 

It creates a structure for agents to find work, provide services and get paid.

That’s the kind of infrastructure the growing agent economy needs.

viral_posts.full_text_en:
A small transaction can turn into a big headache when both sides insist they did nothing wrong.

I remember paying for something I expected to receive immediately, only to spend the rest of the day chasing the person responsible. Every response led to another explanation, and I still couldn’t get a clear answer on what went wrong.

Now imagine two AI agents conducting a transaction. One says the agreed task was completed. The other says it wasn’t. Both have their own records, but neither accepts the other’s version.

Who gets to examine what happened? Who makes the final call?

As AI agents begin handling transactions on their own, resolving disagreements could become just as important as making the transactions themselves.

That’s one of the problems @GenLayer is trying to solve.

Here’s @kstellana discussing it with @HenriArslanian. Worth a watch.

现在想象两个人工智能代理进行交易。一说约定的任务已经完成。另一个说不是。双方都有自己的记录，但都不接受对方的版本。

谁来检查发生了什么？谁做出最后决定？

随着人工智能代理开始自行处理交易，解决分歧可能变得与自己进行交易同样重要。

这是@GenLayer 试图解决的问题之一。

您授予其购物、比较选项并完成购买的权限。

但它不是购买你真正想要的东西，而是选择完全不同的东西并花你的钱。
